item.title: [Recap] Brook Lopez (LAC): Brook Lopez amassed 20 points (8-of-11 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
item.description:
Brook Lopez amassed 20 points (8-of-11 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.

After playing 22 minutes in his first start of the season on Monday, Lopez played 35 in Wednesday’s overtime thriller. Given his production in those two starts and Isaiah Jackson’s inability to avoid silly fouls, Lopez may have the starting center job for the foreseeable future. Jackson, who has committed at least four fouls in six of his eight games, played 13 minutes against the Heat and finished with two points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Darius Garland (LAC): Darius Garland recorded 26 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, seven assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
item.description:
Darius Garland recorded 26 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, seven assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.

By now, it’s known that category-league managers rostering Garland will likely have to punt turnovers. He racked up six turnovers against the Heat, but the Clippers’ guard had his best shooting night this season. In addition to making 10 of 14 shots from the field, he recorded seven assists, making for a decent night at the office.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Rui Hachimura (LAC): Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
item.description:
Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.

Hachimura has gotten off to a relatively slow start with the Clippers, shooting 37.3 percent from the field and 68.4 percent from the foul line. Add inconsistent production in assists, steals and blocks, and rostering Hachimura in some 10-team leagues isn’t worth discussing. He had a productive night against the Heat, with the seven assists being more than double his total entering the night (three). For Hachimura to be someone you can roster in shallow leagues after the Clippers get guys like Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal back, nights like Wednesday have to become the norm.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Giannis Antetokounmpo (MIA): Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, two steals and three blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:
Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, two steals and three blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.

On most nights, fantasy managers can expect Giannis to shoot a high percentage from the field but struggle at the foul line. The opposite happened against the Clippers, with the Heat forward shooting 40 percent from the field and 84.6 percent from the foul line. Antetokounmpo finished with a robust stat line that had everything but a three-pointer. The Heat play two more games this week, starting with the Warriors on Thursday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Davion Mitchell (MIA): Davion Mitchell tallied 11 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:
Davion Mitchell tallied 11 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.

Mitchell’s start to the season has been better than most fantasy managers expected, with the Heat guard providing top-50 per-game value. He couldn’t buy a three-pointer on Wednesday, missing all five attempts, but Mitchell offered excellent production in assists and steals. And even with Wednesday’s poor shooting, Mitchell is still shooting 50 percent from the field this season.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Bam Adebayo (MIA): Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:
Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.

This was a big night for Adebayo, who recorded his first double-double of the season with new highs in points and rebounds. Add in the assists, and it was a good night for those rostering the Heat captain. Even with there still being some bumps the Heat need to smooth over as they work Giannis Antetokounmpo into the fold, Adebayo has been close to a top-25 player in 12-team leagues. That’s encouraging, to say the least.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Klay Thompson (MIA): Klay Thompson finished Wednesday’s overtime win over the Clippers with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and eight three-pointers.
item.description:
Klay Thompson finished Wednesday’s overtime win over the Clippers with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and eight three-pointers.

Thompson had his best game of the season on Wednesday, shooting 8-of-17 from beyond the arc. His last three-pointer was the most important, as the Heat guard/forward hit one from the left corner with one second remaining in overtime to give Miami the win. Inconsistent in his first five games, Thompson has scored at least 19 points in three straight. Could he be returning to fantasy relevance? The Heat play two more games this week, so it may not be a bad time to stream Klay if you need three-pointers.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA

item.title: [Recap] Naji Marshall (DAL): Naji Marshall produced 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Naji Marshall produced 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.

The Mavericks had no answer for Victor Wembanyama and looked set to get blown out. However, Marshall got going in the second half, shooting 7-of-9 from the field and scoring 17 points. Marshall remains a player who can be rostered in deep leagues, even though he’ll come off the bench on most nights.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Cooper Flagg (DAL): Cooper Flagg finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds and five assists.
item.description:
Cooper Flagg finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds and five assists.

After shooting 3-of-19 from the field in Monday’s loss to the Kings, Flagg got off to a terribly slow start on Wednesday. The reigning Rookie of the Year missed all seven of his shots in the first quarter and started 1-of-11 from the field. The good news is that Flagg shot 6-of-8 the rest of the way. Add in the rebounds and assists, and the final stat line was solid, but category managers would have wanted to see more defensive stats.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kyrie Irving (DAL): Kyrie Irving amassed 29 points (9-of-27 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Kyrie Irving amassed 29 points (9-of-27 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Zuby Ejiofor (ATL): Zuby Ejiofor got 11 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals, and a three in 17 minutes against the Wizards.
item.description:
Zuby Ejiofor got 11 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals, and a three in 17 minutes against the Wizards.

The big man from St. John’s had an impact off the bench in this game and was a big factor in why the Hawks got big leads when the bench was in the game. Asa Newell (toe) left the game early and Jock Landale (hip) is already out, so if you wanted to stream in Zuby in deeper redraft leagues, he could have some value for rebounds. In dynasty leagues, you should be happy that he had this performance and flashed what he might be capable of with more minutes.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Onyeka Okongwu (ATL): Onyeka Okongwu had a good 14 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 16 rebounds, four assists, two steals, a block and two 3-pointers in 120-105 win over the Wizards.
item.description:
Onyeka Okongwu had a good 14 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 16 rebounds, four assists, two steals, a block and two 3-pointers in 120-105 win over the Wizards.

Okongwu has been mildly disappointing this season, so it was good to see him have a good game. He got some more stocks which have been lacking at this point. The minutes aren’t going anywhere, so he should continue to have this role barring injury. In dynasty, if he were to ever get traded, his role could be in jeopardy given the fact that he’s an undersized center who doesn’t defend at a super high level.

item.title: [Recap] Dyson Daniels (ATL): Dyson Daniels put up 8 points (4-of-13 FGs), a career high 17 rebounds, and eight assists on Wednesday against the Wizards.
item.description:
Dyson Daniels put up 8 points (4-of-13 FGs), a career high 17 rebounds, and eight assists on Wednesday against the Wizards.

Dyson didn’t score the ball, but he did have a career high 17 rebounds in this game. Dyson’s offense hasn’t gotten back to where it was in his third year, and the lack of a three-point shot will hinder him, but the defense has been awesome, and he’s been what you would’ve hoped for when you drafted him with most of his value coming from steals and good rebounds from a guard.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Kingston Flemings (ATL): Kingston Flemings had 14 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Wizards.
item.description:
Kingston Flemings had 14 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Wizards.

In his first start of his career, he played well and you felt his imprint on the game. It was said on the broadcast that it was CJ McCollum’s idea for Kingston to start and get into a rhythm. It is notable that Kingston played 23 minutes when CJ played 25 minutes. His ability to collapse a defense with his speed was on full display. We’ll see if this is a permanent change, but he clearly looked good in this game.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] AJ Dybantsa (WAS): AJ Dybantsa had 9 points (4-of-12 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, and three assists on Wednesday.
item.description:
AJ Dybantsa had 9 points (4-of-12 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, and three assists on Wednesday.

The Hawks clearly bothered him with their physicality where he missed several buckets around the rim. A lot of his recent value was coming from shooting 93% at the free throw line and he shot 1-of-4 in this game. He will have better performances than this and once he gets used to more of the NBA physicality, he’s going to be a really good player. His athleticism and size allow him to do things that very few players in the league can do.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Kyshawn George (WAS): Kyshawn George with a monster 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, and three 3-pointers in the 120-105 loss to the Hawks.
item.description:
Kyshawn George with a monster 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, and three 3-pointers in the 120-105 loss to the Hawks.

Kyshawn has fit right into his role in the starting lineup and has been a very impactful and important player on this Wizards team. He impacts winning, doesn’t do more than is required, and will do whatever the team asks him to do. He was one of the only players on the Wizards that could hit 3’s in this game with the team going 6 of 26 from three. (23.1%)

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Isaiah Jackson (LAC): Isaiah Jackson finished Monday’s loss to the Raptors with 19 points (9-of-11 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer.
item.description:

Inconsistent as a starter in the Clippers’ first six games, Jackson was moved to the bench on Monday. The decision could have been matchup-based, but Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue stuck with Brook Lopez (12/6/1/1/1 with one three-pointer) as the starting center after Toronto ruled out Jakob Poeltl. Jackson didn’t let the demotion get him down, as he recorded a season-high point total and matched his previous high in rebounds. Simply put, even if Jackson continues to come off the bench, those rostering him shouldn’t throw in the towel.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kobe Sanders (LAC): Kobe Sanders produced 26 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Raptors.
item.description:
Kobe Sanders produced 26 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Raptors.

The Clippers didn’t have Derrick Jones Jr. or Rui Hachimura for Monday’s game, so Sanders made his second start of the season. The second-year wing had the best night of his NBA career, dropping a career-high 26 points. Sanders scored 13 points in both halves, but he may have run out of steam late. Shooting 1-of-5 from the field, Sanders scored five points in the fourth quarter, and the Clippers shot 30.4 percent as a team. That’s how a team goes from leading by 13 to losing by seven.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Scottie Barnes (TOR): Scottie Barnes accumulated 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 8-of-15 FTs), 15 rebounds, eight assists and two steals in Monday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:

Barnes appeared to aggravate his sore left hip during the third quarter, but he returned to the game after some time on the bench. And it’s a good thing he did, as the Raptors forward was outstanding in the fourth quarter. Barnes recorded 15 points, eight rebounds, one assist and two steals in the quarter, helping the Raptors erase a 13-point deficit to win by seven. Barnes struggled at the foul line, but that was his only negative on his final stat line.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: [Recap] RJ Barrett (TOR): RJ Barrett tallied 26 points (10-of-19 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:

Barrett scored 16 points in the first half of Monday’s game, shooting 7-of-9 from the field. The overall stat line was good, except for one category: free-throw percentage. Barrett is shooting a career-worst 58.8 percent from the charity stripe this season, a number that has done his category league value no favors. That said, Barrett is a career 69.5 percent shooter, so it may not be too surprising that he’s started slowly in that regard.

item.description:
Immanuel Quickley accounted for 12 points (3-of-13 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.

Quickley has made at least three three-pointers in four straight and five of six games this season. That, along with the rebounds and assists, was the positive from his performance on Sunday. However, Quickley shot poorly against the Lakers, dropping his field-goal percentage to 37.6 percent for the season. It certainly isn’t impossible for a guard to provide solid value despite a low field-goal percentage, but fantasy managers want to see Quickley shoot better than he has.

item.description:

item.description:

item.description:

That isn’t necessarily bad, but not sharing the floor with a lead guard as talented as Haliburton lowers Siakam’s ceiling. item.description:
